thread:
Jordan Li: Hi folks, I moved from OR to WA and just tried to book a pediatrician for my kid. The provider is listed as in-network on the ZenithCare search, but when I gave the clinic my new Redwood plan info they say the claim would be OON. Bummer. Anyone know next steps?

Maya - People Ops: Sorry you're hitting that. Two quick possibilities: 1) provider directory stale (common), or 2) NPI/TIN on file doesn't match the clinic billing group so carrier sees them as out-of-network. Do you have the clinic's billing NPI or the billing phone?

Jordan Li: I have the billing NPI and their office billing contact. Clinic said their TIN changed last month. I can DM the NPI to avoid posting here.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: please do not post SSNs or full member ID in channel. Use DM or the Benefits Portal support form for sensitive info.

Jordan Li: DM'd the NPI and the screenshot of the ZenithCare directory showing them as 'In Network'.

Provider Ops: Thanks Jordan. We'll open a provider discrepancy with ZenithCare. If the clinic recently changed their TIN they need to re-attest with the carrier. Typical fixes: carrier updates directory (2-6 weeks) or provider updates their billing taxonomy.

Ava (Carrier Liaison): From carrier side: when provider's TIN changes we treat billing groups as new entities until we map NPIs. We can do mapping quicker if the clinic sends a letter on letterhead or a W9 showing the new TIN linked to the billing NPI. If Jordan wants, we can accept an email from the clinic billing office and expedite review.

Maya - People Ops: Jordan, two options: 1) ask the clinic to bill under the old TIN for retroactive claims (if they still accept), or 2) get the clinic to submit the W9/email to ZenithCare and we'll flag it as an in-network directory correction so future claims process correctly. For the immediate visit, if they insist on OON, save the itemized superbill/EOB and we'll help submit an appeal or negotiate.

Jordan Li: Appreciate it. I'll ask the clinic to email the W9 to Ava and will keep the superbill if they bill me OON. One question: if carrier updates and approves network mapping, will they reprocess prior claims automatically?

Ava (Carrier Liaison): We can reopen and reprocess claims in most cases if the service dates fall after the effective network mapping date and the clinic provides documentation showing billing group continuity. We'll confirm after we review the W9. Expect ~10 business days after we receive documents.

Maya - People Ops: Thanks all. Jordan, ping here once the clinic emails Ava and we'll monitor. If anything gets billed to you in the meantime, upload receipts to Benefits Portal > Claims Help and tag us.
